subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should OpenClaw standardize a machine-readable Skill Workshop lifecycle contract in core, and if so should it be OpenClaw-native, AISP reference-only, or external ClawHub/bundle-owned?
rationale: The contract would describe security-sensitive write, scan, approval, rollback, and target-boundary rules, so automation should not choose its authority or home without maintainer intent.

options.title: OpenClaw-native contract first
options.body: Add a docs/tests-owned OpenClaw-native contract or fixture that mirrors the current service behavior, with AISP only as illustrative context.

options.title: Reference package outside core
options.body: Keep core unchanged and publish an AISP or bundle-style reference through ClawHub unless a missing core validator API is identified.

options.title: Defer contract work
options.body: Keep the existing docs, schemas, and tests as the only contract until a concrete validator or trace consumer needs a new artifact.

recommendation.title: OpenClaw-native contract first
recommendation.body: Add a docs/tests-owned OpenClaw-native contract or fixture that mirrors the current service behavior, with AISP only as illustrative context.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced the current Skill Workshop proposal lifecycle and owns the strongest history signal for deciding whether a formal contract should mirror or extend it.
